function: Joint load-balanced user association, BS beamforming and RIS phase-shift design by a graph neural network (p. 1).
system: Downlink multi-cell: 2 BSs with 4x4 UPA, 4 passive phase-only reflecting RISs of 4x4 elements, 6 single-antenna users, 28 GHz mmWave, 400 MHz (p. 12).
method: Heterogeneous bipartite GNN with message-passing MLPs; unsupervised sum-rate loss plus cross-entropy regularization toward collision-avoidance labels; centralized offline training, distributed inference (pp. 8, 10).
data_channel: Custom simulated mmWave geometric channel, L=5 paths, Rappaport path loss, LoS probability of Samimi; random channels and locations per sample; 1,280 independent test samples (p. 12).
test_conditions: Trained at K=6 users and P_b=20 dBm; tested on K=5 to 10 users and 5 to 25 dBm without retraining or fine-tuning; same channel statistics (p. 15).
baselines: Classical: centralized AO (WCS, FP, CCM), local ZF with matching-game association and CCM, Max-SINR with MRT with/without RIS; learned: per-node fully connected network (FNN) (p. 12).
metrics: Sum rate (bps/Hz), load-balancing violation, CPU inference time, signaling overhead in symbols (p. 15).
complexity: Inference order O(TL(4NB+2MJ+8NK+2BK+(4N+n_m)n_m)); CPU time 0.0024 s versus 4.18 s for Global FP at N=16, M=16 (pp. 11, 15).
q1_support: p. 12: "We adopt the following path loss model [45]." The channel is a custom geometric mmWave simulator (p. 4, model [33]) with random channels and user locations; no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 15: "the proposed GNN has strong generalization ability to different numbers of users" - the model trained with K = 6 is tested with K from 5 to 10 without re-training or fine-tuning.
q3_support: p. 12: "Centralized AO: The centralized algorithm in Section III" (non-learned) and p. 12: "fully-connected neural network (FNN)" (learned); both are compared on sum rate in Figs. 9-12 (p. 14-15).
q4_support: p. 11: "The total GNN inference computational complexity is" O(TL(4NB+2MJ+8NK+2BK+(4N+n_m)n_m)); p. 15: "We compare the CPU running time (inference time) of the" proposed GNN with the benchmarks.
q5_support: p. 12: "channels and user locations are randomly generated for each sample" - simulated data; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: Included, area 3: the GNN learns BS beamforming and RIS phase shifts jointly with user association (above PHY), so it passes the above_phy check by the joint-decision rule. q1=0: custom simulator (Akdeniz-type mmWave geometric model, Rappaport path loss, Samimi LoS probability), not 3GPP or measured. q3=1: the FNN is a standard fully connected network on the same problem, but it is built with the same MLP structure as the GNN without message passing (could be read as an ablation); reviewer to confirm. Conclusion (p. 16) says the GNN needs re-training under different channel statistics.
